### Introduction to Sustainable Development

The opening session introduces the foundational concept of sustainable development, its historical development, and the
global challenges it responds to, closing with a first reflection on the relevance of these concepts in participants'
own context.

:::

---

## Session Overview

| | |
|---|---|
| **Format** | Self-paced online module (structure can be adapted for a live/synchronous session) |
| **Duration** | Approx. 90-100 min self-paced (equivalent to a 2h live session) |
| **Preparation for participants** | None (opening session of the course) |

---

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this session, participants will be able to:

1. Define sustainable development and its core principles.
2. Identify key challenges that sustainability aims to address.
3. Discuss the relevance of sustainable development in their own national context.

---

## Session Outline

::: {.session-topics}

**1. Introduction** (3 min)
: Welcome, course outline, learning outcomes.

**2. Opening reflection** (5 min)
: "Earth from space" impulse.

**3. Defining Sustainable Development** (10-12 min)
: Brundtland definition, the three dimensions, Agenda 2063, the SDGs.

**4. Exercise: relevance of SDGs** (8 min)
: How the SDGs, or other national frameworks, relate to participants' own work.

**5. Sustainability Challenges** (10 min)
: Overview of the global challenges sustainable development responds to.

**6. Reflection: challenges in context** (15 min)
: Sustainability challenges in participants' own national/local context.

**7. Sustainability Theories and UN Conferences** (20-25 min)
: Historical development of sustainability thinking and the milestone UN conferences.

**8. Key messages and FAQ** (5 min)

**9. Reflection: key takeaways** (10 min)

**10. Course project introduction** (10 min)
: Introduction to the overall course project (ESD Action Plan) and the task after Session 1.

:::

## Preparation tasks & learning activities

::: {.callout-note .callout-before appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Before the session**

None required. Optional: think of a recent local or global event that made you reflect on sustainability, to bring
into the opening exercise.
:::

::: {.callout-tip .callout-during appearance="simple" icon=false}
**During the session**

- Complete the "Earth from space" opening reflection.
- Work through the SDG/other national framework relevance exercise.
- Complete the national/local context reflection.
- Complete the closing key-takeaways reflection.
:::

::: {.callout-warning .callout-after appearance="simple" icon=false}
**After the session**

Task after Session 1, review of course content: reflect on how sustainable development is currently integrated into
your own teaching practice, evaluate your existing course content and syllabi, and identify areas for strengthening
this integration. This feeds into the overall course project (ESD Action Plan).
:::

## Recommendation for facilitation

- Use an interactive polling tool (e.g. Mentimeter) for the "Earth from space" word-cloud opening in a live session.
- Keep the SDG relevance exercise open-ended rather than pre-selecting example goals, so participants from different
  disciplines can each anchor it to their own field.
- Given how much content the theories section covers, split it into two shorter learning units (historical milestones
  1970-2000; contemporary frameworks 2009-2023) rather than one long block.
- For the Ethiopia/Kenya pilot cohorts, pairing the UN SDGs with the AU Agenda 2063 resonated well as a regionally
  grounded complement to the global framework. When adapting this course for participants elsewhere, look for a
  comparable regional or national framework to pair with the SDGs, since Agenda 2063 will not be equally relevant to
  all users of this course.
